questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Primarily, I wanted a destination, where I could find enough courses in English. Furthermore, due to COVID restrictions at the time of my application, I wanted to stay within Europe. Additionally, Amsterdam's departement of logic is really good so I also wanted to experience that.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Some were easy. Other were hard. So it depends on what aspect of the arrival I needed information about. UvA were not that good in getting information out such that you had a lot of time to respond to it. However, this were due to personal issues for the coordinator. We were informed of this. They were really good at helping if some information were lost after the arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had two international coordinators, which helped with the practicalities and if at any time during the stay we needed to talk to someone then we could contact them. Then we also had the UvA homepage.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy. I tried on my own, but ended up getting an offer through UvA.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You are very much on your own, so invest time into the community around you. For me it was really nice to know some of the people living close to me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Where I were, it was not very nice. However, I know some other students, who got a pretty good place. But all in all the housing were not ideal.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To get accepted you needed to send proof of enrolment at UCPH. Then after you were enrolled, you needed to make sure that you could login through SIS and mail. Then you needed to go through an application formula, which involved a copy of your passport, language test, course selection ect. You were overall guided well through that part.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Primarily the UvA homepage, but you could also get in contact with the international coordinator. However due to personal circumstances, she were not present for the last part of June and the beginning of August.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Overall quite successful. I only had issues with one course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time, research the courses well and read up on the limitations on UvA's homepage.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were very hard. Others were easier. However, in general I will say that the level corresponds to the level in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They were more or less identical. You had lectures and in-class sessions with other students. However, sometimes there were sometimes, where you had classes with the professer themselves.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Graph Theory and Algorithms, Numerical Linear Algebra, Dynamic and Distributed Programming, Introduction to Quantum Computing and Bayesian Statistics for Machine Learning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Graph Theory and Algorithms and Introduction to Quantum Computing as I found them the most fun and interesting. Additionally, I think they will be the courses, I use the most afterwards.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The cost of travelling and moving there. Especially for Christmas, where I wanted to go home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food were a bit cheaper. Otherwise the prices are more or less the same as in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: ESN was really great, but it was very late that I was introduced to anything at Science Park and it seemed like, for many, that most groups had an academic purpose.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN facilitated a lot of experiences, get together, outings ect., which were amazing. Furthermore, at science park there were a gym, where you had options for student memberships ect.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Be a part of ESN and volunteer there. For me it gave an amazing network of people, that I still talk to. Especially also in the beginning, where you do not know anyone.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit The Haag and Zaandam to see the windmills.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I had to get used to how direct and 'impolite' many Dutch people are. Other than that the culture were not that different from Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make it your goal to talk to them at every class and do the in-class session's assignments in groups. For me it felt very uncomfortable at first, but slowly they warmed up to me. So more or less keep trying. It takes time.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Other than how direct they say things, they are also quite reserved like Danes. This can be hard when you need to find a group for uni ect.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really came to like the directness. You could get to your points quicker and less misunderstandings occured.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be aware that in the beginning you may feel very much alone and on your own. Enjoy the little things and take it one day at a time. 
2. Get a museum card and be curios. They are really starting to reflect on their past and that is really interesting. 
3. Insist on talking to the locals. You will learn a lot about yourself and your own culture.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you need to figure out a lot on your own, but don't be too afraid to send an email to the coordinator.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The personal growth. I have gained a huge insight into myself and my own values. It is like I could see my own culture through someone else. Additionally, I have become much more confident in myself and my own abilities.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling lonely. Especially in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
